item.title: AI Builders Fellowship 2026 (Internet Archive Canada x BC + AI)
item.description:
Organisation: Internet Archive Canada (IAC) in partnership with BC + AI

Location: Remote, open to builders anywhere in the world. Optional in-person showcase at Futureproof Festival in Vancouver, Canada on 28 October 2026 if the project is ready.

Award: $5,000 award for one selected builder. No application fee.

Duration: Six-week build, 1 September to mid-October 2026, remote, with support from BC + AI throughout

Deadline: Closed 21 Aug 2026

A $5,000 fellowship to spend six weeks turning a very large Canadian public archive into something new. THE MATERIAL: Internet Archive Canada's Government Publications collection, part of the Democracy's Library project, holding over 104,000 text items, roughly 22.1 million scanned pages and about 48.25 TB of Canadian public-record material, browsable at archive.org/details/governmentpublications. WHAT TO BUILD: deliberately open-ended. The call names a search tool that answers a real question with page-level citations, a timeline tracing one policy across decades of government language, and a sonic or visual piece built from archival material, but explicitly invites work nobody has thought of yet. The requirements are that it is useful, that it is imaginative, and that the code is open source when it is done. ORIGIN: the fellowship came out of conversations between BC + AI's Kris Kruger and IAC executive director Andrea Mills about treating a public archive as material for new work rather than only something to preserve. IAC brings the archive, BC + AI brings a community of builders used to working in public. ELIGIBILITY: anyone, anywhere in the world; one builder is selected. APPLICATION: a specific project description grounded in the collection, a phase-by-phase work plan for the six weeks, and a success metric, submitted at bc-ai.ca/fellowship/apply. KEY DATES: applications close 21 August 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific; fellow selected by 31 August; build runs 1 September to mid-October; showcase at Futureproof Festival in Vancouver on 28 October 2026 if the project is ready.

item.title: Wilson Center Research Fellowship, 2027-2028 Class
item.description:
Organisation: Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars

Location: Remote for the duration of the fellowship, with two required trips to Washington DC (at the start and the end) for which travel costs are covered.

Award: USD 10,000 per month for a twelve-month fellowship, plus covered travel for the two required trips to Washington DC. No application fee.

Duration: Twelve months, 1 June 2027 to 30 May 2028

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

The Wilson Center, the congressionally chartered nonpartisan policy research institution in Washington DC, awards 10 to 20 research fellowships for its 2027-2028 class. Fellows conduct research and write in their areas of interest while interacting with policymakers in Washington and with other fellows. The Center accepts policy-relevant, nonpartisan proposals that address key foreign policy challenges confronting the United States and the world, and projects must align with at least one of the Center's four scholarship pillars: strategic competition, economic statecraft, TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION, and regional scholarship. The technology and innovation pillar is the relevant route for AI governance, emerging technology and digital policy projects, which the Center also supports through its Science and Technology Innovation Program. Fellows work remotely for the duration of the fellowship; the Center covers travel costs for two required trips to Washington DC at the beginning and the conclusion of the term. The stipend is USD 10,000 per month for the twelve-month term, which runs 1 June 2027 to 30 May 2028. ELIGIBILITY: academic candidates need a PhD in hand and either a published book or monograph beyond the dissertation, or a substantial body of research articles (five or more) in reputable peer-reviewed journals. Non-academic applicants (practitioners, journalists, public intellectuals) need at least ten years of relevant experience and a record of substantial policy impact. There is no citizenship restriction, but English proficiency is required. Applications, including letters of recommendation, must be submitted online via Interfolio by 11:59pm ET on 30 September 2026. Questions: fellowships@wilsoncenter.org. NOTE: this is an open-topic foreign policy fellowship, not an AI-specific one; the technology angle depends on how you scope the proposal.

item.title: AIAF Fellowship, Autumn 2026
item.description:
Organisation: AI Alignment Foundation

Location: Fully remote for the 8-week research period; hybrid Demo Day in Los Angeles with travel covered for those attending in person. Non-US applicants welcome if available for Pacific Time meetings.

Award: USD 12,000 stipend paid in two installments, plus a compute budget. Travel covered for in-person Demo Day attendance. No application fee.

Duration: 8 weeks full-time at 40 hours per week, starting 8 September 2026

Deadline: Closed 17 Aug 2026

An eight-week full-time empirical AI alignment research programme run by the AI Alignment Foundation, with a dedicated research manager, mentorship from senior researchers, compute and infrastructure, culminating in a Demo Day where fellows present their work. Fellows receive a USD 12,000 stipend paid in two installments plus a compute budget. The programme is fully remote for the research period; Demo Day is hybrid in Los Angeles and travel is covered for fellows who attend in person. ELIGIBILITY: open to all career stages, including recent PhDs, graduate students, self-taught researchers and career-changers, but candidates need a strong machine learning background, demonstrated engagement with alignment research, prior independent research output, and the ability to work autonomously. Non-US applicants are welcome provided they can make Pacific Time meetings; current graduate students may apply if they can confirm availability. This is explicitly a technical programme: the foundation says policy-focused applicants should not apply. SELECTION: all applications are reviewed, qualified candidates advance to a technical test, and finalists are interviewed, with decisions expected by early September. Applications close 17 August 2026 (Anywhere on Earth); the programme starts 8 September 2026.

item.title: Center for Humane Technology: Emerging Voices in AI and Society Fellowship (Inaugural Cohort)
item.description:
Organisation: Center for Humane Technology (CHT)

Location: Remote, 10 hours/week overlapping with EST required.

Award: $30,000 fixed stipend paid in three milestone-based tranches. No application fee.

Duration: 6 months: September 14, 2026 through March 18, 2027. 15 hours per week.

Deadline: Closed 12 Jul 2026

CHT's inaugural Emerging Voices in AI and Society Fellowship places 3 fellows (one per focus area) in a 6-month, part-time program to develop rigorous public-impact research and writing on how AI is reshaping society. Fellows choose from 5 focus areas: (1) AI and Cognition — what AI does to human judgment, critical thinking, and intellectual independence; (2) AI and Relationships — AI's effects on intimacy, companionship, and social bonds; (3) AI and Surveillance — how AI enables monitoring, tracking, and control; (4) AI and Spirituality — AI's intersection with meaning, transcendence, and religious practice; (5) Inside the Machine: AI From a Technologist's Perspective. Up to 2 focus areas per application. DELIVERABLES: one flagship research piece, report, or long-form essay for public impact; 1-3 op-eds (placed in target outlets or CHT Substack); one podcast appearance (Your Undivided Attention or equivalent); cohort meetings and bi-weekly check-ins. SUPPORT: bi-weekly guidance from Senior Director of Strategy and Impact; editorial, communications and graphic design support; media training and PR placement support; CHT email address and Slack access; listing on CHT's public fellows page. WHO SHOULD APPLY: mid-career researchers (psychology, sociology, philosophy, cognitive science, communications, STS), policy analysts, journalists covering tech and society, civil society advocates, or technologists with insider perspective. Strong preference for those with a public writing track record (op-eds, Substack, peer-reviewed work) and some public presence. HOW TO APPLY: 1-2 page research proposal per topic (up to 2), CV/resume (2 pages max), 2-minute video explaining fit, writing sample. Deadline: Sunday 12 July 2026, 11:59pm EST.

item.title: Longview Philanthropy: Digital Minds Research Fellowships 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Longview Philanthropy

Location: Worldwide / remote or institutional (grant-eligible countries listed in application form)

Award: $55,000–$120,000/year through a university, or $80,000–$150,000/year direct stipend; plus research budget (10% of salary), conference travel, and compute resources where applicable. No application fee.

Duration: 1–2 years. Second year conditional on continuing to meet programme requirements.

Deadline: Closed 10 Jul 2026

Longview Philanthropy Research Fellowships support scholars pursuing research on the potential consciousness, sentience, moral status, and legal position of AI systems. AMOUNT: $55,000–$120,000/year (through a university, with 10% research budget and standard fringe benefits), or $80,000–$150,000/year (direct stipend, with suggested 5–10% allocation for research and travel). Compute resources available for machine learning research. Invitation and funding to attend the annual Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy Summit at NYU. ELIGIBILITY: must have or be expected to receive a doctoral degree in computer science, neuroscience, a related technical discipline, law, medicine, or applied social science by September 2027 or fellowship start date (exceptions for equivalent research experience); fellows arrange their own institutional affiliation; fellowship may be conditional on institutional affiliation or attendance at events. SELECTION CRITERIA: demonstrated interest in digital minds and its relation to AI risk; evidence of research promise (publications, academic achievements, references). DURATION: 1–2 years; second year conditional on ongoing programme requirements. AREAS OF INTEREST: introspection, welfare measurement, interpretability, model character, correlates of consciousness, valence research, governance frameworks, legal and political responses to potentially sentient AI. Deadline: 10 July 2026. Required application materials: CV, description of possible research directions (~1,000 words), intended outcomes, what you would do without this fellowship (~150–400 words), career goals (~300 words). Questions: digitalminds-rfp@longview.org. Apply at https://www.longview.org/request-for-proposals-research-and-applied-work-on-digital-minds/.

item.title: Longview Philanthropy: Digital Minds Career Development Fellowships 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Longview Philanthropy (in collaboration with Future Impact Group)

Location: Worldwide / remote

Award: Stipend calibrated to the duration of the award, cost of living and the recipient's prior experience, plus additional funding for research or logistics on a case-by-case basis. No application fee.

Duration: Variable; calibrated per award

Deadline: Closed 10 Jul 2026

Funding to develop a career working on the potential consciousness, sentience, moral status or welfare of artificial intelligence systems (digital minds). The fellowships aim to grow a new generation of researchers, policymakers, communicators, entrepreneurs and practitioners working on digital minds and AI sentience issues. EXAMPLE CANDIDATES: a current or planned PhD or other degree student seeking financial support to study digital minds issues; a technical AI researcher who wants to explore research topics, attend events and meet organisations in the space in order to select a high-impact role; or a communications professional pivoting into digital minds work (for example running surveys or building experts' platforms). SUPPORT: a stipend calibrated to award duration, cost of living and prior experience, plus additional case-by-case funding for research or logistics. APPLY by 10 July 2026. Questions: digitalminds-rfp@longview.org.

item.title: Heinrich Boell Foundation: Global Majority AI Fellowship 2026 (UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance)
item.description:
Organisation: Heinrich Boell Foundation Washington, DC

Location: Geneva, Switzerland (first session); applicants must be civil society experts based in countries receiving Official Development Assistance (ODA)

Award: Travel and logistics reimbursement only: international flights, airport transfers, and up to three nights of accommodation in Geneva. Conference registration, accreditation and access facilitated; promotion on the Foundation's social-media channels before the Dialogue. NO artist fee, stipend or honorarium.

Duration: First session 6-7 July 2026 in Geneva (2 days), with continued engagement through the second session in New York in May 2027

Deadline: Closed 18 May 2026

Fellowship from the Heinrich Boell Foundation Washington, DC supporting Global Majority civil society experts to participate in the first session of the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance in Geneva (6-7 July 2026), with continued engagement through the second session in New York in May 2027. The Global Dialogue, established by the UN General Assembly in August 2025 under the Global Digital Compact, is a new multilateral forum to ensure AI governance reflects the priorities of all nations and that the benefits of AI are shared broadly. THEMATIC CLUSTERS at the Global Dialogue: AI opportunities and implications (social, economic, ethical, cultural, linguistic, technical dimensions); bridging AI divides (capacity-building, access, digital foundations); safe, secure and trustworthy AI (interoperability and compatibility of approaches); respecting, protecting and promoting human rights (transparency, accountability, human oversight). The fellowship aims to amplify Global South voices on issues of core relevance to the global green movement - human rights, bias, ecology, labor, conflict - and to improve gender balance in global AI governance. ELIGIBILITY: emerging or experienced leaders working on AI governance, digital rights, data justice, environmental and climate justice or related fields with a focus on the global dimensions of AI policy - activists, local officials, students, researchers and technologists - based in a country receiving Official Development Assistance. WHAT IS EXPECTED: travel to Geneva and active participation on 6-7 July 2026; fellows are encouraged to participate in activities ahead of the 2027 New York session; provide a short statement on the issues they hope to see addressed at the Dialogue and reflect on the experience; engage actively with the Foundation over social media before, during and after the Dialogue; be part of an emerging network of civil society experts working to strengthen AI governance globally. PROCESS: applicants must (1) apply to the official UN AI Dialogue 2026 Call for Participation Support, AND (2) send application materials to the Foundation via Drew.Mitnick[at]us.boell.org and Mariama.Balde[at]us.boell.org. Materials: standard resume/CV (max 2 pages, including country of residence and gender; no photo or marital status) plus a motivational statement (max 300 words) on the biggest challenge for AI governance right now, how to address it, current steps being taken, and how Dialogue participation will advance those goals.
